Bundled collections, concrete user structs, and opaque bounds dispatch reads and writes through one complete checked `__getitem__`/`__setitem__` contract: exact target, executable result type, typed raising effect, receiver/argument access and caller places, captures, generic value parameters, reference result, and setter write-back. Augmented nominal subscripts evaluate receiver/index sources once and retain call-local adaptations and effects. A value getter runs after the RHS, then the operator and independently adapted setter; a getter-mutated caller place is reloaded before that setter. A mutable-reference getter establishes its handle before the RHS and writes through it with no setter. Retained reference arguments are checked for invalidation after all source-ordered index arguments have been evaluated. Call-less `Index` and `Slice` instructions retain an explicit intrinsic dispatch family instead of asking the VM to infer one from runtime representation. Variadic structs use current Mojo's `__getitem_param__` hook; its source index is reused as a compile-time value argument without becoming an ordinary runtime argument. Reference-returning index and slice results retain a hidden loan-bearing handle when chained as another receiver/place; shared field projections, Mojito-only Pointer/private-storage projections, and reference-return forwarding extend the materialized handle and remain valid direct bindings or `mut`/`ref` call places. Ordinary value reads from nominal elements retain the selected accessor contract and copy lifecycle. The earlier `__getitem__` spelling for dependent Tuple accessors remains a source-compatibility fallback. Plain subscript assignment on a receiver with no `__setitem__` writes through a mutable-reference-returning `__getitem__` (upstream Array's contract): the getter contract is selected once, the right-hand side types against the referent, and lowering finishes with a direct reference write; an immutable receiver or immutable-reference getter rejects.
